title: Memory conductor: per-variant working-set sculpting for long-context variants
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Long-context requests (>= 4k) for certain model variants (Llama 70B-Long, Mistral-16k quantized, Qwen-32k) regularly trigger higher GPU working-set contention and KV residency churn, leading to elevated tail latencies and sporadic OOMs under continuous batching. Existing generic memory profiles are conservative and cause under-utilization for quantized variants or overcommitment for wide-token distributions.

Goal: Implement a 'memory conductor' — a per-variant, sequence-aware profile selector that sculpts allocation/residency and KV-slicing strategies at request time to optimize GPU working set, reduce OOM risk, and improve throughput while preserving tail-latency SLOs. The conductor should: select a memory footprint profile based on model variant, quantization type, and live sequence-length histogram; adjust KV slice residency heuristics; and suggest batching knobs (max batch size, max latency window) to the serving runtime.

Plan:
1) Profile representative variants under synthetic and sampled production workload to extract working-set curves (resident bytes vs prefix length) and KV hot-key distributions. Target variants: Llama-70b-long (fp16), Mistral-16k (q4_0/q4_1), Qwen-32k (q5). Use the profiling harness from ENG-31472 plus new long-seq driver to sweep prefix sizes 512, 2k, 4k, 8k.
2) Derive compact per-variant 'conductor profiles' (small table: breakpoints for prefix lengths, target KV residency fraction, preferred slab sizes). Store as JSON blobs consumed by runtime decision layer.
3) Implement runtime selector hook (non-blocking): on request enter, lookup variant+quant+estimated-seqbucket and attach profile hint to allocation path. This should be opt-in via config flag runtime.memory.conductor.enabled.
4) KV adjustments: implement dynamic kv-slice residency toggles — prefer coarse-grained residency for quantized Mistral when prefix < 2k, and aggressive residency for Qwen wide contexts. Also add a soft-eviction policy that avoids evicting prefix frames if new sequence length is predicted to grow.
5) Continuous batching integration: add conductor suggestions to batching policy (max_batch_by_variant, latency_window_hint) so the batching layer can favor smaller batches for variants with tight working sets.
6) Testing and rollout: unit tests for selector logic, microbench harness for throughput/latency, canary rollout on dedicated pool with telemetry for OOMs, tail P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec per-GPU.

Success metrics: reduce production OOM incidents for long-context traffic by >= 80% in canary; increase average tokens/sec per-GPU for targeted variants by >= 8% without P99 latency regression > 5%; maintain parity for short-context workloads.

Risks & trade-offs: additional selector overhead on request path (measure impact < 0.3 ms), configuration complexity for ops, risk of mis-calibrated profiles causing memory fragmentation. Fallback: runtime.memory.conductor.enabled=false restores previous behavior.

Artifacts: profiling dashboards (Grafana link stub: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/longctx-memory), design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Memory+Conductor+Design, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1848, profiling harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/profiling/tree/memory-conductor
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can load per-variant profiles and attach profile metadata to requests in the serving runtime
Microbench: targeted variants show >=8% tokens/sec/GPU improvement on 4k and 8k synthetic traces vs baseline profiles
Canary: OOM count for sampled long-context traffic reduced by >=80% compared to baseline over 24h
No P99 latency regression >5% for end-to-end request latency on canary compared to control (same timeframe)
Integration tests for KV soft-eviction logic and selector unit tests are present and green
Documentation updated: runtime config guide, conductor profile format schema, and rollout playbook
Config flag runtime.memory.conductor.enabled defaults to false and is controllable per-pool via console
Observability: dashboards show per-variant residency, eviction events, and conductor decisions for troubleshooting
comments: 2025-11-10 Sofia Patel: Initial ticket created after incidents on 2025-11-08 where two dedicated pools serving 4k+ contexts reported OOM spikes. Attached initial profile sketches and sampling plan.

2025-11-12 Carlos Mendes: Run profiling harness against Mistral-16k q4_0 and Qwen-32k q5; attached results to Grafana panel. Observed that Mistral quantized variants have a flatter working-set curve but higher fragmentation. Need slab-size tuning.

2025-11-15 Evan Liu: Review note — ensure selector decision is idempotent and lightweight. Avoid synchronous calls to config store on hot path; cache profile blobs in-thread with TTL. Also suggested a lightweight checksum for profile compatibility.

2025-11-17 Priya Raman: Bench results v1: Mistral-16k q4_0 on 8k traces showed 12% tokens/sec improvement but P99 increased by 3.8%. Draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1848 submitted for initial review.

2025-11-19 Marta Kozlova: Design feedback — add a conservative 'safe-mode' profile that runtime can switch to if eviction rate spikes. Also suggest telemetry counters for profile-hits and profile-fallsbacks.
2025-11-20 Carlos Mendes: Implemented safe-mode and TTL cache; updated PR with unit tests for selector. Asking infra to schedule a canary on dedicated-pool-3 (ticket INF-7420).

2025-11-22 QE (Jun Park): Running canary smoke: 24h ingestion shows 86% reduction in OOM incidents for sample workload; tail latency stable within target. Captured logs and csvs in /artifacts/canary/ENG-512999/.

2025-11-23 Security (Anya Ivanova): Quick review — conductor profiles are metadata only, no secrets. Recommend an ACL on who can write profiles to the configuration store. Marking security_review_required=false.

2025-11-24 Sofia Patel: Next steps: polish docs, finalize rollout playbook, schedule runtime-1.20 inclusion. Reminder: add a small migration script to convert legacy profile format to conductor schema.
